purpose: Assess the 2015 Aritao and Bambang River biodiversity assessment as a source for Region II freshwater fish coverage, while keeping unnamed fish counts and interview recollections out of species occurrence data.

source.title: Physico-Chemical, Biological and Anthropogenic-Related Attributes of Cagayan River Sub-tributaries in Nueva Vizcaya, Philippines
source.publication: International Journal of Scientific Engineering and Research, Volume 5, Issue 2, February 2017, pages 89-95
source.license: The PDF footer states Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY); it does not specify the license version.

studyScope.samplingDescription: The paper reports three sampling sites along Aritao River and two along Bambang River, with three 100 m transects per site. GPS was used to identify geographical locations, but station coordinates were not found in the published text reviewed.
studyScope.regionalRelationship: The paper places both study rivers among Cagayan River sub-tributaries in Nueva Vizcaya, within the wider Magat/Cagayan basin context. This is site-level context, not basin coverage.

reviewedEvidence.publishedFishTable: Table 3 reports the label 'Fish' with a value of 3 for each river. It does not name the taxa or explain the count unit sufficiently for this review to treat the values as a species list.
reviewedEvidence.observedCatchNarrative: The paper says tilapia was caught during the survey, without a scientific name, station, specimen identifier, or event-level association.
reviewedEvidence.historicalInterviews: The narrative recounts local names including freshwater shrimp, ayungin, and paltat as part of interview-based memories of earlier fishing. These are not dated study samples or verified species identifications.

qualityAndReuseLimits: The reviewed publication does not provide scientific fish names, specimen catalog numbers, accession identifiers, or fish-specific station records; no fish species occurrence can be created from this paper alone.
Although GPS is described in the methods, no station coordinates were found in the published text reviewed. Do not derive points from town names or maps.
The paper's environmental measurements and historical interview statements are source-period context, not present-day water-quality or food-safety advice.
The CC BY footer is recorded as printed; confirm the applicable license version and scope at the publisher before reusing substantial content or figures.
nextAction: Seek station-level fish identification sheets, photos, vouchers, or follow-up publications from the authors and Saint Mary's University research laboratory. Continue discovery in other Region II rivers and lakes in parallel; require scientific names, source-linked collection events, locality evidence, and reuse checks before species projection.
